text.p: Iberia's is meeting other shareholders in the loss-making Venezuelan airline Viasa to push forward a restructuring plan, an Iberia spokesman said.

The Spanish airline which owns 45 percent of Viasa, has already invested heavily to cover the affiliate's losses now wants the other major shareholder Fondo de Inversiones de Venezuela to contribute towards the cost of reducing the company's workforce as part of a plan to bring it into profit.
Iberian chairman Xabier de Irala is in Venezuela this week to try and advance the proposals, the spokesman added.

Besides shedding unprofitable routes, Iberia thinks Viasa needs to cut its 2,200 workforce by 15 to 20 percent and is trying to persuade the Fondo to pay for the job cuts -- estimated to cost some $18 million -- and provide a further $4 million to streamline Viasa's operations.

Iberia for its part is willing to write off $21 million of the $140 million Viasa owes it and to cut Viasa's interest payments on the rest of the debt by $3.5 million and give it free of charge $1.5 million worth of aircraft maintenance.
Iberia invested an initial $73.5 million to buy its stake in Viasa in 1991 and another $43.6 million later to cover losses in 1991 and 1992, and it is unwilling to stump up further capital.
Since it was privatised, Viasa has produced a steady, although shrinking, stream of losses totalling $200 million in the last five years.
But Iberia, which is responsible for managing Viasa, said restructuring now will quickly bring it into profit. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
